items.title: upstream tracking: prompt_toolkit CPR queries not suppressed on Windows — stacked status frames under PowerShell/ConPTY

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Context

This is an **upstream tracking issue** for a known prompt_toolkit behavior, NOT a Hermes code bug.

Hermes intentionally keeps prompt_toolkit's default output on Windows (`_terminal_may_leak_cpr()` returns `False` for `sys.platform == "win32"`, `cli.py:3732`). The classic-CLI `Application` is constructed without an explicit `output=` argument, so prompt_toolkit's stock ConPTY/console path emits CPR (`ESC[6n`) queries (`_request_absolute_cursor_position`, `_on_resize`, `terminal_size_polling_interval` default 0.5s, pt 3.0.52 docs).

On **Windows PowerShell / ConPTY / conhost**, the CPR reply (`ESC[<row>;<col>R`) is frequently **delayed, dropped, or misrouted**. A leaked reply is parsed as literal text into the input buffer; during a resize storm the renderer's scroll-up reflow pushes previously-rendered full-width status-bar rows into scrollback = the stacked/ghost status frames.

## Known upstream references

- **pt #13870** — CPR race on SSH/slow PTYs (same mechanism, Hermes references this)
- **pt #56747** — no-console-flash on Windows
- **pt #29 / #1675 / #1933** — resize scroll-up reflow that Hermes monkey-patches in `cli.py:17599-17641`
- **pt #48309** — background redraws fighting Windows Terminal auto-scroll

## What Hermes already does (mitigations in place)

- `erase_when_done=True` on Application construction (cli.py:17574) — prevents frozen chrome on exit
- `_output_screen_diff` monkey-patch (cli.py:17599-17641) — suppresses pt's resize "reserve vertical space" scroll
- `_strip_leaked_terminal_responses_with_meta` (cli.py:3804) — scrubs leaked CPR/mousereports from input
- `_invalidate()` throttle (cli.py:4872) — 0.25s default, prevents excessive redraws
- `display.cli_refresh_interval` config (default 0 = disabled) — controls PT idle redraw cadence

## What Hermes does NOT do (gap)

- Suppress CPR on Windows (by design — "no native-Windows Application coverage yet")
- Reap orphan CLI `python.exe` children (separate issue, see #86204)

## Recommendation

If Hermes wants to fix Driver 2, add Windows CPR suppression (return a CPR-disabled `Vt100_Output` from `_select_classic_cli_pt_output` on win32). That is a separate PR from the reaper-gap fix.

Until then, this is a known limitation documented as an upstream tracking issue — not something Hermes can fix unilaterally without a prompt_toolkit behavior change or a Hermes-side Windows CPR suppression implementation.

## Cross-reference

- Driver 1 (Hermes reaper gap): #86204
- PR #86123 (pid_alive refactor, separate from both drivers)

## Summary

The Hermes **desktop client** on Windows is broken after the last **2 consecutive updates** (2026-07-31 and 2026-08-14). After each update the desktop app's backend exits with code 1, the app can't restart itself ("Reopen Hermes to finish"), and the update pipeline falls back through git → ZIP, both of which fail on `WinError 32` file locks. The app only comes back after manually closing and reopening it.

This is the desktop-app variant of the Windows update lock chain already tracked in #63717 and #68760, but with an additional failure: the desktop update hand-off finishes with a **manual action** instead of restarting the app, and the backend repeatedly exits (1) during the update window.

## Environment

- **OS:** Windows 11 (git-bash/MSYS shell)
- **Hermes:** git install at `C:\Users\admin\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent` (venv), branch main, HEAD `de0abc061` (2026-08-14)
- **Desktop build stamp:** `desktop-build-stamp.json` builtAt 2026-08-14T08:43:15Z, sourceMode=false
- **Python:** 3.11.15 (venv), uv 0.12.0 (managed)
- **Update dates:** 2026-07-31 00:38, 2026-08-14 16:41 and 23:57 (two attempts on the 14th)

## What happened (from `~/.hermes/logs/`)

### 1. Desktop backend exits (1) repeatedly during the update window

`desktop.log`:
```
[hermes] [updates] restart: Updating Hermes — this window will close and the updater will open. Don't reopen Hermes yourself; it restarts automatically when the update finishes.
[hermes] [updates] state.db pre-flight: size=175353856, headerOk=true, ...
[hermes] [updates] venv shim unlocked; safe to proceed
[hermes] Hermes backend exited (1)
[hermes] [boot] An update is finishing — Hermes will start automatically when it completes…
[hermes] [updates] launched repo hand-off script: ...\scripts\desktop-update\windows.ps1 (branch main); exiting desktop to release venv shim
[hermes] [updates] detached update finished with manual action (branch main): Update complete. Reopen Hermes to finish (it could not restart itself).
```

The same `Hermes backend exited (1)` line appears ~10 times across the two update events; the app does **not** restart itself after the update completes — the user has to manually close and reopen it every time.

### 2. `hermes update` fails: git install → ZIP fallback → both hit WinError 32

`update.log` (2026-08-14 16:41):
```
⚠ hermes.exe is locked by another process; scheduled replacement on next reboot.
error: failed to remove file `...\hermes-agent\venv\Lib\site-packages\../../Scripts/hermes.exe`: The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process. (os error 32)
⚠ Git update failed: Command '[...\uv.exe', 'pip', 'install', '-e', '.']' returned non-zero exit status 2.
→ Falling back to ZIP download...
✗ ZIP update failed: [WinError 32] The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process: '...\hermes-agent\ui-tui' -> '...\hermes-agent\ui-tui.hermes-update-old'
```

Same pattern in `hermes-update.log` (2026-07-31): `hermes.exe` locked by another process (os error 32) → git update failed → ZIP fallback → `WinError 32` on `ui-tui` rename.

### 3. Secondary noise during boot

`desktop.log`:
```
[hermes] [boot] could not read served dashboard token (Hermes backend): 404: {"error":"Headless backend (hermes serve): web UI disabled — use `hermes dashboard` for the browser UI."}
⚠ Deprecated .env settings detected: TERMINAL_CWD=... (move to config.yaml terminal.cwd)
```

## Expected behavior

- `hermes update` / desktop self-update completes on Windows **without** WinError 32 lock failures (detect/kill the processes holding `hermes.exe` and `.pyd`/`ui-tui` files, or use a staged/reboot-safe replacement).
- The desktop app restarts itself after the detached update finishes instead of requiring a manual reopen ("it could not restart itself").
- No `Hermes backend exited (1)` during the update hand-off window.

## Workaround used

Close the desktop app fully, run the update, then manually reopen — works, but every update requires this manual dance and the ZIP fallback still leaves a partially-updated tree.

## Related

- #63717 — Windows: Hermes Desktop update failures (comprehensive diagnostic, 7 correlated root causes)
- #68760 — hermes.exe locked during `hermes update` on Windows (WinError 32)

items.title: Dragging files/images onto the composer input shows a no-drop cursor; drop-to-attach no longer works
items.body:
## Summary

Dragging files/images from the OS onto the composer input shows a no-drop cursor and the drop-to-attach flow no longer works. Regression: this used to work; the only current workarounds are copy-paste or the + (attach) button.

## Root cause

- The composer input has full drag-and-drop handling (`handleInputDragOver` in `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-composer-drop.ts`: `preventDefault + stopPropagation + dropEffect='copy'`), but it is gated on `dragHasAttachments()` matching — which checks `dataTransfer.types` for `Files` or an app-specific MIME.
- A window-level `dragover` listener from react-dnd's HTML5Backend (mounted for the file tree and similar components) intercepts non-internal drags: when the drag is not a react-dnd internal drag, it calls `preventDefault` and forcibly sets `dataTransfer.dropEffect = 'none'`.
- When the dragged content doesn't match `dragHasAttachments` (e.g. in-app images or web-page image drags whose `types` don't include `Files`), the input handler returns early without intercepting; the event bubbles up to the window-level listener, gets forced to `none`, and the no-drop cursor appears.
- The input handler itself has not changed since it was extracted (6/30 refactor); the behavior change comes from the interaction between the window-level listener and the input handler's early-return gate.

## Suggested fix

- Have the input `dragover` handler also `preventDefault + stopPropagation` for non-`Files` drag types, so the event never reaches the window-level listener.
- Or make the window-level listener skip cases where the drag target is the composer/chat area instead of forcing `none`.

items.title: Desktop: sameCronSignature drops pin/archive-only session updates

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug

On current `main`, Desktop session refreshes discard pages whose only changes are row-state flags. `sameCronSignature()` in `apps/desktop/src/lib/session-signatures.ts` compares content and recency fields, but not `pinned` or `archived`.

`refreshSessions()` therefore keeps the previous atom when a fetched page changes only one of those flags:

```ts
return sameCronSignature(prev, next) ? prev : next
```

The backend write succeeds, but `$sessions` can retain the stale row indefinitely for an idle conversation. For pinning, that stale row is then consumed by `session-pin-sync`; once its confirmation guard expires, an old `pinned: true` row can resurrect an item the user already unpinned. The same omission makes archive-only changes invisible to this signature gate.

## Distinct from earlier pin races

This is not the earlier pull-before-push race fixed by #75973 for #74570. It is also one layer above the write-confirmation guard added by #77170 for #76919: the guard has a valid confirmation path, but the page carrying the confirming `pinned` value is filtered out before it can reach the reconciler.

## Reproduction

1. Start with an idle pinned conversation, so no title, preview, count, or timestamp field is moving.
2. Unpin it and confirm the backend row changes to `pinned = 0`.
3. Let session refresh return the same row with only `pinned` changed.
4. The page is judged signature-equal and discarded; the cached row remains `pinned: true`. After the write guard expires, a later reconciliation can re-adopt that stale value.

A focused unit test that changes only `pinned` fails on current `main`; the equivalent archive-only test fails as well.

## Expected behavior

`sameCronSignature()` should treat both `pinned` and `archived` as significant row state, with regression tests for pin-only and archive-only deltas. This causes one atom update per deliberate pin or archive action and does not reintroduce ordinary session-page churn.

## Proposed fix

PR #86218 implements the minimal fix and regression coverage:

- compare `session.pinned === other.pinned`
- compare `session.archived === other.archived`
- add pin-only, archive-only, and unchanged-state tests

No additional `session-pin-sync` retry behavior is required for this issue unless a fresh reproduction remains after the confirming page is allowed through.

items.body:
## Summary

Desktop app v0.20.1 (macOS, LOCAL mode, 2+ profiles): switching to a non-primary profile spawns that profile's pooled backend serve, but the renderer **never establishes a WebSocket connection to it**. The sidebar project tree therefore falls back to the last-known tree of the PRIMARY profile. Clicking any primary-profile project inside the secondary profile's view auto-switches the app back to the primary profile.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have 2+ local profiles (primary + secondary) with distinct projects.
2. Open the app; the primary tree renders in the sidebar.
3. Switch to the secondary profile via the rail.
4. Observed: the sidebar STILL shows the primary profile's projects (project-tree grouping). The secondary profile's own projects never appear.
5. Click any primary-profile project → the app switches the active profile back to primary (pill changes) and opens the session.
6. Workaround found: switching sidebar grouping to **"updated"** (recent) shows the secondary profile's sessions correctly — that list path IS profile-scoped. So session data routing is fine; only the project tree is wrong.

## Evidence

- Fresh app restart, 3 serves spawned at boot:
  - primary serve: holds the app's ESTABLISHED connections (2).
  - secondary serve: spawned as `--profile <secondary> serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0`, LISTENING on its ephemeral port, but **0 ESTABLISHED connections** from the app (`lsof -nP -a -p <pid> -iTCP`).
- External WS probe of the secondary serve + `projects.tree` returns the CORRECT tree (its own projects only). The backend is healthy; the renderer just never dials it.
- Persists across full app restarts (Cmd+Q), not just a reload. Not the all-profiles browse mode (`hermes.desktop.showAllProfiles` = false in localStorage).

## Expected behavior

Switching to a profile shows that profile's own project tree in the sidebar.

## Environment

- macOS 15.7.5 (arm64), Hermes Desktop v0.20.1
- Local profiles only, no remote gateway / no per-profile connection overrides

## Code trail (source at current HEAD)

- `apps/desktop/src/store/profile.ts` — `selectProfile()` → `ensureGatewayProfile(name)`
- `apps/desktop/src/store/gateway.ts` — `ensureGatewayForProfile()` → `openSecondary()` → `desktop.getConnection(profile)` → `entry.gateway.connect(wsUrl)`; on failure `scheduleReconnect(entry)` runs and `setActive(key)` STILL executes, so `$activeGatewayProfile` moves to the secondary profile while its socket is dead.
- `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` — `ensureBackend()` returns the pooled `connectionPromise`; `spawnPoolBackend()` self-probes `/api/ws` before declaring ready, so the descriptor looks valid.
- `apps/desktop/src/store/projects.ts` — `refreshProjectTree()` → `activeProjectsContext()` → `activeGateway()`; with a dead secondary gateway the refresh fails and the cached (primary) tree is kept by design ("failure leaves the cached tree intact so the sidebar doesn't flicker").

- #77005 (remote mode, same symptom family: sidebar shows launch profile's projects)
- #75308 (projects_db_path per-profile)
- #74551 (wrong profile backend after reconnect)

items.title: [desktop] Review 'commit and open PR' can route to wrong keep-alive session

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug description

When multiple Hermes Desktop chat sessions are mounted as keep-alive tabs, clicking **Review → “Let Hermes commit and open a PR”** can route the generated submission to a different chat session than the one visible at click time. The UI may also jump to that unrelated session, while the intended visible session receives nothing.

This is especially risky because the generated prompt asks the agent to commit changes and open a pull request, so cross-session delivery can execute repository actions in the wrong conversational/project context.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop with at least two established chat sessions mounted as tabs in the main chat area.
2. In a local Git repository, create an uncommitted change and open the right-hand Review pane.
3. Keep an unrelated session mounted, then make the repository-specific session visible.
4. Click **“Let Hermes commit and open a PR”** in the Review pane.
5. Observe the selected tab and inspect the sessions’ messages.

## Expected behavior

- Exactly the visible chat composer at click time receives the Review submission.
- No hidden keep-alive composer receives it.
- No unrelated session is activated.
- Delivery happens at most once.

## Actual behavior

- A physical click can switch the Desktop to an unrelated mounted session.
- The intended visible session may receive no Review prompt.
- Read-only comparison of the Desktop message database confirmed that the intended A/B fixture sessions did not receive the Review submission in the failing run; historical attempts placed the generated Review prompt in the unrelated session lineage.

## Source-level diagnosis

The Review action uses a window-level composer submit event with a broad `target: "main"`. Multiple keep-alive composer instances subscribe to that global event. Routing based only on a broad target and subscriber state is vulnerable to tab-switch timing and does not strongly bind the click to one concrete mounted Chat surface.

A robust fix should capture the visible composer surface synchronously at click time and require the receiving subscriber to match that exact, non-null surface identity, in addition to target, pane visibility, and input-disabled guards. It must also fail closed for new sessions that do not yet have a persisted session ID.

## Verified against latest `main`

Checked on 2026-08-15 before filing:

- installed source: `91e550b0cf7822875fad537c238d584aedd2dcc5`
- latest `origin/main`: `a90d5369f76c87c98547d2e283aa26d5cfabf322`
- commits between them: 252
- the Git blobs for `composer/focus.ts`, `use-composer-submit.ts`, `composer/scope.tsx`, `chat/index.tsx`, and Review `ship-bar.tsx` are byte-for-byte identical at both revisions
- no Desktop commit in that range changes `requestComposerSubmit`, `SUBMIT_EVENT`, `onComposerSubmitRequest`, `usePaneVisible`, or `data-composer-target`

Latest `main` still dispatches the Review request as a window-level event with `target: "main"`, while the receiver only checks `target === "main" && !inputDisabled`; it does not bind delivery to the visible pane or to one concrete mounted Chat surface. Updating through those 252 commits therefore does not contain an equivalent fix.

## Environment

- Windows 11
- Hermes Desktop v0.20.0 (+252), upstream build `91e550b`
- Reproduced with two keep-alive Desktop sessions and a local-only Git fixture with no remote

## Related work

- Candidate fix: #85911
- Related but distinct: #66661 covers rejected-submit text being restored into the wrong composer; this report concerns Review-pane submit routing before/while submission is dispatched.

The candidate PR has passing automated routing tests, lint, type checks, build, and the full Desktop UI test suite, but manual end-to-end acceptance of the final candidate is not complete. Please do not treat the PR as a verified fix solely from this report.

labels.name: duplicate

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Bug description

On Windows, the Desktop app's backend (`hermes serve`, launched with `HERMES_DESKTOP=1`) kills **every** running gateway process when it starts up — including a gateway that was installed/started independently via `hermes gateway install` (which registers the `Hermes_Gateway` scheduled task) or `hermes gateway start`.

Concretely: a user runs the gateway as a background service (scheduled task) so messaging platforms (e.g. Weixin) stay online. Every time they open the Hermes desktop app, the backend starts and silently kills that gateway. `hermes gateway status` then reports "No gateway process detected", and the Weixin connection drops. There is no shutdown/exit line in `logs/gateway.log` — the process is SIGTERM'd (then SIGKILL'd) by the reap.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows, run `hermes gateway install --start-now --start-on-login` (registers the `Hermes_Gateway` scheduled task and starts the gateway detached, `HERMES_GATEWAY_DETACHED=1`).
2. Confirm it's running: `hermes gateway status` → `✓ Gateway process running`.
3. Launch the Hermes desktop app (`hermes desktop`), wait for the backend to boot.
4. Run `hermes gateway status` again → `✗ No gateway process detected`.
5. `logs/gateway.log` shows the gateway connected (`[Weixin] Connected account=<hex>`) and then nothing — no shutdown/exit path ran.

## Expected behavior

A gateway that is *supervised* (launched detached by the Windows scheduled task / service wrapper) should be left alone. The desktop backend's orphan-reap should only clean up gateways that a *previous* desktop `serve` session forked and abandoned.

## Actual behavior

The desktop backend reaps the independently-managed gateway on every startup.

## Root cause

`hermes_cli/web_server.py` `_lifespan` runs on every desktop-backend startup:

```python
if os.getenv("HERMES_DESKTOP") == "1":
    from hermes_cli.gateway import _reap_unsupervised_gateway_orphans
    _reap_unsupervised_gateway_orphans()
```

`hermes_cli/gateway.py::_reap_unsupervised_gateway_orphans` gates itself on a service supervisor:

```python
if supports_systemd_services():   # False on Windows (no systemd)
    return False
orphans = find_gateway_pids(exclude_pids=own)   # returns ALL gateway PIDs
```

On Linux/macOS, `supports_systemd_services()` is True and the reap is a no-op because systemd/launchd supervise the gateway. On Windows there is no systemd, so the function proceeds and reaps **every** `gateway run` process — including the scheduled-task gateway, which is *supervised* by the Windows Task Scheduler (the `Hermes_Gateway` task) and launched with `HERMES_GATEWAY_DETACHED=1`.

The distinction between "desktop-forked orphan" and "detached/supervised gateway" is recoverable from the process environment: the scheduled-task/service wrappers set `HERMES_GATEWAY_DETACHED=1` on the gateway's environment, while the desktop's own fork does not.

## Proposed fix

Skip detached (service/scheduled-task-launched) gateways in the orphan reap, detected via `psutil.Process(pid).environ()`:

```diff
--- a/hermes_cli/gateway.py
+++ b/hermes_cli/gateway.py
@@ -1523,6 +1523,25 @@
         except OSError as exc:
             print(f"Failed to kill PID {pid}: {exc}")
     return killed
+
+
+def _is_detached_gateway_process(pid: int) -> bool:
+    """Return True when a gateway PID was launched service-style (detached).
+
+    The Windows scheduled-task / service wrappers (e.g. ``Hermes_Gateway``)
+    set ``HERMES_GATEWAY_DETACHED=1`` in the gateway's environment so it can
+    absorb console controls. Such a gateway is *supervised* by its launcher,
+    not an orphan, so the desktop backend's orphan reap must not kill it.
+    Best-effort: on any failure we conservatively return False so the legacy
+    reap behaviour is unchanged.
+    """
+    try:
+        import psutil  # type: ignore
+        env = psutil.Process(pid).environ()
+    except Exception:
+        return False
+    detached = (env or {}).get("HERMES_GATEWAY_DETACHED", "").strip().lower()
+    return detached in {"1", "true", "yes", "on"}
+
 
 def _reap_unsupervised_gateway_orphans(extra_exclude: set | None = None) -> bool:
@@ -1578,6 +1578,10 @@
         # find_gateway_pids() includes no-supervisor `gateway restart` runtimes
         # for the current profile when no systemd supervisor is present.
         orphans = [p for p in find_gateway_pids(exclude_pids=own) if p and p > 0]
+        # A detached gateway (service/scheduled-task-launched) is *supervised*
+        # by its launcher, not an orphan. Reaping it would kill the user's
+        # independently-managed gateway whenever the desktop backend starts.
+        orphans = [p for p in orphans if not _is_detached_gateway_process(p)]
     except Exception:
         return False
     if not orphans:
```

Note: `psutil` is already a dependency (imported lazily elsewhere in `hermes_cli/gateway.py`). The detection is best-effort and falls back to the legacy behaviour when the target process environment can't be read.

## Environment

- **OS:** Windows 11 (zh-CN locale)

### Problem or Use Case

I'm running hermes-agent with DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 locally with ik_llama.cpp on an old server CPU. 
Works fine actually. But it's slow enough to see what's happening in the background.

**Problem:**
The new DeepSeek V4 models have aggressive context compression. If existing context gets changed, the entire context or large parts of it have to be reloaded. That should not be a problem in this usecase, but it is. Prompts by hermes-agent don't always end on a space or a newline. The next context of a prompt or a tool call might just gets stuck to the previous without newline and spacing. 

**Tokens are not letters.**
So if you stick a new word directly onto the last word of the previous context without clear spacing, the last few letters of the existing context and the new letters might create a different token. And just like that the existing context has been corrupted.
So quite often the model may consider the last token of the previous context to have been altered, causing the entire context or big chunks of it to get dumped and reloaded. Especially tool calls cause this quite frequently. 
That really starts to hurt once you're above 100k tokens of context.

### Proposed Solution

The easiest and most reliable way around this is to always have a newline (/n) at the end of every prompt.

So I fixed this by telling hermes to alter its code, making sure that every prompt sent to the LLM has a newline (/n) as suffix. If it doesn't, it's added. 

Result: Speed increased instantly manyfold on long contexts, much less tokens need to be computed and every other model still works fine.

items.body:
## Summary

Hermes Kanban workers set `TERMINAL_CWD` at runtime to the task workspace, but CLI startup reports that value as a deprecated `.env` setting on every worker run.

## Reproduction

On Hermes `v2026.8.13`, dispatch a Kanban task with a directory workspace. Its task log begins with output equivalent to:

```text
Deprecated .env settings detected:
TERMINAL_CWD=/workspace found in .env — this is deprecated.
Then remove the old entries from <profile>/.env
```

There is no `TERMINAL_CWD` entry in the root, profile, or project `.env` files. `hermes_cli.kanban_db._default_spawn()` sets `env["TERMINAL_CWD"] = workspace` deliberately. `hermes_cli.config.warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()` checks only `os.environ`, so it cannot distinguish that supported runtime injection from a dotenv-loaded legacy value.

## Impact

- Every ordinary Kanban worker writes a false warning to its task log.
- Operators are told to edit a file that does not contain the setting.
- Warning-based soak/health monitoring cannot distinguish configuration drift from normal worker startup.

## Expected behavior

Warn only when the deprecated key was actually loaded from a dotenv source. Runtime-owned `TERMINAL_CWD` used to bind a Kanban worker to its workspace should remain supported and silent.

One possible approach is for dotenv loading to record the keys/sources it supplied and have `warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()` consult that provenance instead of treating every environment value as dotenv-derived.

items.title: cron scheduler: create_execution failure strands job in running set forever ('already running — skipping' every tick)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-automation
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect CI, automerge, label sync, or maintainer automation

items.body:
## Summary

In `cron/scheduler.py` `_submit_with_guard` (~5299-5317):

```python
if not try_register_running_job(job_id):
    ... return None
execution = create_execution(job_id, source="builtin")   # can raise — no cleanup
...
try:
    return pool.submit(_run_and_release)
except Exception as submit_err:
    release_running_job(job_id)   # only the submit path releases
```

`create_execution` runs **after** `try_register_running_job` succeeds but **outside** the `try` that releases on failure. `create_execution` can genuinely raise (`cron/executions.py` ~27-29: `mkdir` OSError on unwritable disk; `sqlite3.connect` + schema init can exhaust busy_timeout → `OperationalError`).

If it raises:
1. `job_id` stays in `_running_job_ids` forever — every subsequent tick hits "already running — skipping" (INFO only), so the job is dead **until the gateway restarts**, with no ERROR-level signal.
2. The exception propagates through `tick()`'s dispatch loops (~5344-5367, no try wrapper), so **all remaining due jobs this tick are never submitted**. Recurring jobs lose a cycle; one-shots additionally stay blocked by their persisted `run_claim` until its TTL (default 30 min).

## Suggested fix

Wrap the ledger write:

```python
try:
    execution = create_execution(job_id, source="builtin")
except Exception as exc:
    release_running_job(job_id)
    logger.error("Job '%s': execution ledger write failed, skipping this fire: %s",
                 job.get("name", job_id), exc)
    return None
```

## Trigger

executions.db write failure (disk full, `~/.hermes/cron/` permission change, NFS lock timeout) coinciding with a tick that has due jobs.

Found auditing v0.20.1 (v2026.8.13).

labels.name: duplicate

## Summary

`tools/file_operations.py` (~1480-1492) counts lines with `wc -l`, which counts newline characters. A file with 5 newline-terminated lines plus a final unterminated line reports `total_lines: 5` while actually having 6 lines of content. When the read window reaches EOF, `sed -n` still prints line 6 and `_add_line_numbers` numbers it — so the model sees `6|...` in content but `total_lines: 5, truncated: false` in metadata: self-contradictory, and any paging math based on total_lines is off by one. The same file already has a last-byte probe (`tail -c 1 | wc -l`, ~1499-1503) that could be reused.

## Suggested fix

After computing `total_lines` (~1480-1486), if the file's last byte is not `\n`, increment by 1. The `offset > total_lines > 0` guard (~1516) and `truncated` (~1489) then behave correctly automatically.

## Trigger

Reading any text file lacking a trailing newline (hand-written configs, some generators).

labels.name: duplicate

items.body:
## Summary

`tools/file_tools.py` uses host-side `os.path.getmtime(resolved_str)` / `os.path.exists(resolved_str)` for read dedup (~1796-1799, ~1935-1940), post-write timestamp updates (~2088), `_check_file_staleness` (~2117), and the not-found cache existence guard (~1297). When a task runs on a docker/ssh/modal backend, `resolved_str` is a path in the container/remote namespace, but the stat hits a same-named **host** path.

Two outcomes:
- Normal case (no such host path): `OSError` is swallowed; dedup/staleness/negative-cache guards silently no-op on remote backends — a silent feature loss contradicting the comments.
- Pathological case (host file exists at the same path, e.g. SSH to shared storage or overlapping bind mounts): the remote file changed but the host mtime didn't → `read_file` returns an `unchanged` stub and feeds **stale content to the model as if current** — the exact failure this mechanism exists to prevent.

## Suggested fix

Early-return guard before those host stats: skip bookkeeping/comparison when the task's backend is non-local (e.g. `_terminal_env_type_for_task(task_id) == "ssh"` or container paths), letting reads fall through to full content.

## Trigger

Non-local terminal backend; the pathological branch also needs a same-named host file.

## Summary

`cron/jobs.py` ~2996-3003 (`_get_due_jobs_locked`) persists a fresh `run_claim` for one-shot jobs; but skip/failure paths in `cron/scheduler.py` — `_interpreter_shutting_down` → return None (~5293-5298) and `pool.submit` raising (~5314-5336, which releases the running set and records the failure but never clears the run_claim) — leave the claim in place. On both return-None paths (before ~5298 and in the ~5317 except block), clear `run_claim` for `schedule.kind == "once"` jobs (e.g. a `cron.jobs.clear_run_claim(job_id, expected_owner=...)` using the existing CAS pattern), so the next tick picks them up immediately.

labels.name: comp/agent

## Summary

`batch_runner.py` ~1321-1325: fatal paths `return 1`, but the entry point is `fire.Fire(main)` (~1328-1329). python-fire does not propagate the callee's return value as the process exit code — `return 1` is merely serialized/printed, and the process exits 0. Replace the error-path `return 1` / bare `return` in `main` with `raise SystemExit(1)` (Fire lets SystemExit propagate with its code), or wrap: `if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main())` with plain argparse-style dispatch instead of Fire for the exit-code path.

items.title: cli: signal-armed outer exit watchdog can hard-kill the process while cleanup is mid-flight

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

`cli.py` ~1121-1159 (`_arm_exit_watchdog_on_shutdown_signal`) arms a `2×base` (default 60s) daemon-thread watchdog immediately on SIGTERM/SIGHUP; `_run_cleanup` (~1172) later arms its own `base` (30s) watchdog. The two timers are independent daemon threads with **no disarm/supersede mechanism**. The comment (~1134-1137) claims the outer timer only wins if cleanup never starts — which doesn't hold:

- t=0 signal → outer timer fires `os._exit(0)` at t=60
- Graceful unwind (`agent.interrupt()` → `app.exit()` → prompt_toolkit teardown → atexit chain) takes 30-60s (slow but not stuck, e.g. a finally waiting on non-daemon threads) → `_run_cleanup` starts at t=45 and arms its own 30s budget (to t=75)
- Outer timer fires at t=60, hard-killing cleanup 15s in — killing exactly the data-persistence steps (memory provider `on_session_end`, `flush_pending`) the watchdog exists to protect

## Suggested fix

At `_run_cleanup` entry (after ~1167 `_cleanup_done = True`), record a module-level `_cleanup_started` timestamp/Event; `_watchdog` (~1087) checks it after sleeping, before `os._exit(0)`: if cleanup has started and this timer isn't the one cleanup armed, yield/return and let cleanup's own 30s timer be the backstop. `_arm_exit_watchdog` needs to record which side armed it to distinguish the two.

## Trigger

Graceful-exit duration falling in `(HERMES_EXIT_WATCHDOG_S, 2×HERMES_EXIT_WATCHDOG_S)` — default 30-60s.

Found auditing v0.20.1 (v2026.8.13).

items.title: [Bug] hermes gateway restart crashes with raw PermissionError when XDG_RUNTIME_DIR leaks from another user (su/sudo -u without login shell)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
### Description

`hermes gateway restart` (and any other command hitting the user-systemd preflight) crashes with an unhandled `PermissionError` when the process environment carries an `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` belonging to a *different* user — the classic case being switching from root to the install user without a login shell (`su <user>`, `sudo -u <user>`, `runuser -u <user> --` from a root shell).

### Environment

- hermes-agent 0.20.0 (also verified on current `main` @ a871948), installed via the official one-liner (`git` install method)
- Ubuntu 22.04 server, install user `hermes` (uid 1001), gateway installed as a user-level systemd unit with linger enabled
- Python 3.11.15 (uv-managed venv)

### Reproduction

```
root@host:/root# runuser -u hermes -- hermes gateway restart   # env inherited: XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/0
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/hermes/.hermes/hermes-agent/hermes", line 11, in <module>
    main()
  File "/home/hermes/.hermes/hermes-agent/hermes_cli/main.py", line 12806, in main
    rc = args.func(args)
  File "/home/hermes/.hermes/hermes-agent/hermes_cli/gateway.py", line 6849, in gateway_command
    gateway_command(args)
  File "/home/hermes/.hermes/hermes-agent/hermes_cli/gateway.py", line 7405, in _gateway_command_inner
    systemd_restart(system=system)
  File "/home/hermes/.hermes/hermes-agent/hermes_cli/gateway.py", line 3486, in systemd_restart
    _preflight_user_systemd()
  File "/home/hermes/.hermes/hermes-agent/hermes_cli/gateway.py", line 1975, in _preflight_user_systemd
    if _user_systemd_socket_ready():
  File "/home/hermes/.hermes/hermes-agent/hermes_cli/gateway.py", line 1911, in _user_systemd_socket_ready
    _user_dbus_socket_path().exists()
  File "/home/hermes/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.11.15-linux-x86_64-gnu/lib/python3.11/pathlib.py", line 1235, in exists
    self.stat()
PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/run/user/0/bus'
```

Same crash reproduces via direct call, confirming it is not shell-specific:

```
$ runuser -u hermes -- ./venv/bin/python -c \\
  'from hermes_cli.gateway import _user_systemd_socket_ready; _user_systemd_socket_ready()'
PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/run/user/0/bus'
```

Controls: with `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1001` the function returns `True`; with the variable unset it falls back to `/run/user/{uid}` and also returns `True`.

### Root cause

`_user_systemd_socket_ready()` (hermes_cli/gateway.py:1913 on `main`) does bare `.exists()` calls on paths derived from `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`:

```python
return (
    _user_dbus_socket_path().exists()
    or _user_systemd_private_socket_path().exists()
)
```

`Path.exists()` only suppresses a subset of `OSError` (ENOENT, ENOTDIR, EBADF, ELOOP); **EACCES is raised**. `/run/user/0` is `0700 root:root`, so a non-root process stat-ing `/run/user/0/bus` gets `EACCES` and the exception escapes the preflight. I verified this behavior on Python 3.11, 3.12 (source) and 3.13 — i.e. across the entire `requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.14"` range.

Note the docstring of `_preflight_user_systemd` promises to "raise `UserSystemdUnavailableError` with a precise remediation message" as the terminal failure path — instead the user gets a raw traceback.

The same bare-`.exists()` pattern on `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`-derived paths also exists in `_ensure_user_systemd_env()`, which additionally *trusts* a leaked `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and propagates it into `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`.

### Suggested fix

1. Minimum: make the readiness check return `False` on inaccessible paths so the existing `UserSystemdUnavailableError` path is taken:
```python
def _user_systemd_socket_ready() -> bool:
    try:
        return (
            _user_dbus_socket_path().exists()
            or _user_systemd_private_socket_path().exists()
        )
    except OSError:  # e.g. EACCES on another user's runtime dir
        return False
```
2. Better UX: in `_ensure_user_systemd_env()`, validate the inherited `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (exists, accessible, owned by the current uid) and replace it with `/run/user/{uid}` when it belongs to someone else — then the restart actually *succeeds* after `su`/`sudo -u` instead of just failing cleanly.

Happy to turn this into a PR if the approach sounds good.

items.title: [Bug]: Windows cron script execution uses base Python with PYTHONPATH, ignoring .pth files from editable installs

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
### Bug Description

`cron/scheduler.py::_run_job_script` runs script jobs using `sys.executable`. On Windows environments where a virtual environment was created with `uv`, `_windows_cron_python_invocation` (around line 2162 of `cron/scheduler.py`) bypasses the venv launcher, invokes the base Python interpreter directly, and attempts to re-attach the venv by setting `PYTHONPATH` to its `site-packages`.

However, `PYTHONPATH` entries are standard directory additions on `sys.path`. Python's site initialization does NOT process `.pth` files for paths added solely via `PYTHONPATH` — that only occurs for genuine site directories via `site.addsitedir()`. As a result, every editable package installed in the virtualenv (`pip install -e ...` / `.pth` links) is invisible to cron script jobs, resulting in `ModuleNotFoundError`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a `uv` virtualenv on Windows.
2. Install a package in editable mode (`pip install -e <path>`).
3. Configure a cron script job (`no_agent: true` or python script) that imports the editable package.
4. Execute the cron job via the scheduler.

### Actual Behavior

Under the base interpreter + scheduler's `PYTHONPATH`:
- Standard non-editable packages (e.g. `yaml`): OK
- Root on `PYTHONPATH` (`hermes_cli`): OK
- Editable packages: `ModuleNotFoundError`

### Expected Behavior

Editable packages installed in the virtual environment should be importable by scheduled cron scripts.

### Root Cause Analysis

In `cron/scheduler.py`: `_windows_cron_python_invocation` sets `PYTHONPATH` but does not invoke `site.addsitedir()` on the venv site-packages.

### Proposed Fix

In the script execution runner or Python invocation wrapper, ensure `site.addsitedir()` is called for the virtualenv's `site-packages` directory before script execution, ensuring `.pth` files are processed.

### Affected Component

- Gateway / Cron / Tools
- Operating System: Windows

items.body:
### Bug Description

While investigating gateway supervisor lifecycles on Windows, two detachment diagnostics and lifecycle issues were identified:

1. **`stdin_is_tty` in `gateway-exit-diag.log` is a misleading detachment diagnostic on Windows.**
   `gateway.py:4942` records `_stdin_is_tty = bool(sys.stdin and sys.stdin.isatty())` into every `gateway.start` record. On Windows, `os.isatty()` returns `True` for any character device, and `NUL` / `subprocess.DEVNULL` is a character device. A properly detached child process spawned with `windows_detach_flags()` (`0x09000200`) and `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` reports `stdin_is_tty: True` even though it has no attached console (`GetConsoleWindow() == 0`).
   The field only differentiates `pythonw.exe` (`sys.stdin is None` -> `False`) from `python.exe` (`True`), giving a misleading impression that a detached background gateway process remains attached to a terminal.

2. **Silent breakaway fallback in `_spawn_detached` leaves the gateway attached to launcher Job Objects.**
   In `gateway_windows.py:952-969`, if spawning with `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB` fails with `OSError`, the spawn is retried with `windows_detach_flags_without_breakaway()`. While falling back is reasonable, nothing is logged and no indicator is recorded in `gateway.start`. When launched from environments that use Windows Job Objects (e.g. Electron desktop app, Tauri installer, certain terminal emulators), the gateway silently remains in the parent job object. When the parent job owner exits, the gateway is terminated immediately by Windows with no exit record written to `gateway-exit-diag.log`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. **For `stdin_is_tty`:**
   Spawn a child with `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP | DETACHED_PROCESS` and `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL`. Inspect `sys.stdin.isatty()` — it returns `True`.
2. **For Breakaway Fallback:**
   Launch the gateway inside a nested job object that forbids breakaway. Observe that fallback occurs with 0 log messages and no metadata indicating breakaway failed.

### Expected Behavior

- Diagnostics should accurately report whether a console/TTY is attached on Windows (e.g. via `GetConsoleWindow` or checking `HERMES_GATEWAY_DETACHED`).
- Breakaway fallback should log a `WARNING` and record whether `breakaway` succeeded in the `gateway.start` record.

### Proposed Fix

- In `gateway.py`: Replace raw `isatty()` on Windows with a check using `ctypes.windll.kernel32.GetConsoleWindow()` or `msvcrt`, and record `HERMES_GATEWAY_DETACHED`.
- In `gateway_windows.py`: Log a warning when falling back to `windows_detach_flags_without_breakaway()`, and add a `breakaway: true/false` field to the startup diagnostic payload.

### Affected Component

- Gateway / CLI
- Platform: Windows

items.body:
### Bug Description

`_gateway_provider_error_reply` (`gateway/run.py:522-536`) maps upstream model provider failures to concise, user-friendly chat responses across gateway channels (Telegram, Discord, Slack, etc.). 

It currently contains dedicated branches for:
- Authentication failures
- Provider policy rejections
- Rate limiting (429)

All other errors fall through to the generic catch-all at line 536:
> *"The model provider failed after retries. I kept raw provider details out of chat, check gateway logs for diagnostics."*

For local/self-hosted model deployments (e.g. `llama.cpp`, Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio running locally on `http://127.0.0.1:8033/v1`), the most common failure mode is that the local model server is simply not running or crashed. 
In this scenario, direct network connection errors (`httpx.ConnectError`, `openai.APIConnectionError`, `WinError 10061: target machine actively refused it`) are caught and properly classified in the core conversation loop, but are collapsed into the generic catch-all at the gateway reply layer.

Directing a user on a mobile chat channel (away from the machine) to "check gateway logs for diagnostics" provides no actionable feedback when the server is just offline.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Hermes with a local model endpoint (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:8033/v1`).
2. Stop the local model server process.
3. Send a message to the agent via a gateway channel or a2a.

### Actual Behavior

After retries, the user receives:
> *"The model provider failed after retries. I kept raw provider details out of chat, check gateway logs for diagnostics."*

Underlying error in conversation loop: `APIConnectionError` / `ConnectError` (WinError 10061).

### Expected Behavior

The chat reply should clearly notify the user that the model endpoint is unreachable / not running.

### Proposed Fix

Add a dedicated branch in `_gateway_provider_error_reply` before the catch-all for connection errors (`openai.APIConnectionError`, `httpx.ConnectError`, etc.):

```python
if is_connection_error:
    return f"The model server at {configured_base_url} is not responding — it looks like it is not running."
```

### Affected Component

- Gateway
- Agent Core / Configuration

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop retry of a failed turn silently truncates history via ordinal-only path — row-id guard (#83785) does not cover it

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug Description

With #83785 merged, deliberate edits/rewinds are protected by durable `truncate_before_row_id` addressing + 4018/4030 refusals. But the **retry / plain-resubmit path after a failed turn** still travels the ordinal-only back-compat path, and a stale ordinal mis-aimed a real truncation in production: a retry of a 429-failed turn silently discarded 68 messages (4 user-turns deeper than intended) from the model's context.

This is the residual hole of #82959 (auto-closed by the #83785 merge): the client and server ordinal address spaces had diverged, and because no row id was attached on this path, neither cross-check could fire.

## Incident (2026-08-14, Windows Desktop, kimi-k3 long session with prior in-place compactions)

1. `23:49:36` — user submits a normal new message; agent turn starts.
2. `23:50:21–23:50:47` — turn dies on HTTP 429 after 3 retries (`API call failed after 3 retries ... msgs=602`).
3. `23:53:37` — user re-attempts the failed turn. Gateway log: `prompt.submit: truncating session … history 600 -> 532 messages (ordinal=19)`.
4. **No new user text was persisted with that submit** (verified in `state.db`: the only rows stamped `23:53:37` are rebuild copies of earlier messages).
5. The cut deactivated 68 rows starting from a user message sent at **22:56** — four user-turns *before* the message being retried — silently dropping 3 subsequent user messages plus ~48 min of agent work from the model's active context.
6. The Desktop transcript still shows all discarded messages in original order (renderer state), so from the user's side the history looked intact; the model later discovered side effects (files, wiki edits, background processes) it had no memory of — a confusing divergence.

Data was fully recoverable thanks to `archive_dropped` from #82950 — that safeguard worked exactly as intended.

## Expected Behavior

Any submit that truncates should be addressed durably (row id) regardless of which client path initiates it (edit / regenerate / retry-after-error / plain resubmit with leaked composer state). If a row id can't be supplied, the gateway should refuse rather than trust an ordinal whose address space may have drifted from the renderer's.

## Analysis

- The ordinal the client sent (`19`) was presumably correct in the renderer's *visible* user-message list, but the gateway counts all `role==user` non-`display_kind` rows — after in-place compactions, rebuild copies, and branch hiding, the two lists no longer align, so ordinal 19 resolved to different messages on each side. Exactly the drift #82959 catalogued.
- `planEdit` (use-prompt-actions) attaches `source.rowId` for edits, and the failed-turn case (`isFailedTurn`) deliberately sends **no** truncation — but the observed submit did truncate with an ordinal and no row id, so it came from a path where the truncate state wasn't cleared and no durable id was attached (retry/resubmit with leaked composer rewind state, matching the #82756 mechanism).
- Suggestions: (a) thread `rowId` through retry/resubmit/regenerate paths too; (b) clear composer truncate state when a turn fails; (c) gateway-side strict mode: refuse ordinal-only truncation (`4004`) for sessions whose history carries row ids.

items.title: Strip encrypted reasoning tokens from conversation context on cross-provider delegation and model switch

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Problem

When the model is switched mid-session (e.g. from Anthropic to GPT to GLM via OpenRouter), the conversation history contains encrypted reasoning tokens from the previous provider. These tokens are opaque blobs that only the original provider's API can decrypt. When delegation passes this context to a subagent on a different provider, the new provider rejects the request:

```
HTTP 404: Your request contains encrypted reasoning or compaction content
that was produced under a different model. Encrypted payloads can only be
replayed to the endpoint that created them.
```

This kills all downstream delegation after a model switch. The subagent never runs — it fails before its first API call.

## Root cause

`drop_thinking_only_and_merge_users` (in `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py:1355`) strips assistant turns that contain ONLY thinking/reasoning blocks with no visible content. But it does NOT strip encrypted reasoning blocks from turns that also contain real text or tool calls. Those turns pass through with the encrypted reasoning still attached, and the new provider rejects them.

## Why the encrypted reasoning is not needed

Encrypted reasoning tokens are provider-internal state (Anthropic extended thinking, OpenAI o-series encrypted reasoning). They are opaque to any other provider and to the agent itself. The subagent needs only:

- Plain-text user messages
- Plain-text assistant responses (content + tool calls)
- Tool call results
- The task description (goal + context)

All of these are fully portable across providers. The encrypted reasoning adds zero value to cross-provider calls and actively breaks them.

## Proposed fix

When the provider changes mid-session, or when delegating to a subagent on a different provider, strip all encrypted reasoning/thinking blocks from assistant turns in the conversation context before sending. Keep the plain-text content, tool calls, and tool results intact.

Specifically, in the API message preparation path (before the cross-provider call), for each assistant message that has thinking/reasoning blocks:

1. Remove all blocks of type `thinking`, `redacted_thinking`, `reasoning_content`, `reasoning_details`, `codex_reasoning_items` from the content
2. Keep all `text`, `tool_use`, `tool_result`, and other non-reasoning blocks
3. If the turn ends up with no content after stripping (thinking-only), it gets dropped by the existing `drop_thinking_only_and_merge_users` logic

This makes model switching mid-session safe for delegation, context compression, background review, and any other feature that replays conversation history to a different provider.

## Reproduction

1. Start a session on Anthropic Claude (with extended thinking enabled)
2. Switch the model to GPT-5.6 or GLM-5.2 via OpenRouter mid-session
3. Call `delegate_task` — the subagent fails with HTTP 404 encrypted reasoning error

## Environment

- Hermes agent with OpenRouter as the provider
- Model switching mid-session (Anthropic → GPT/GLM)
- Delegation to subagents on a different provider than the original

items.title: Gateway auto-resume persists an empty user message that triggers Pre-call sanitizer on every subsequent turn

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

When the gateway restarts with a `resume_pending` session (e.g. the daily 05:58 SIGKILL/OOM restart on Termux), `_schedule_resume_pending_sessions` synthesizes an inbound message with empty text. The gateway's resume branch in `gateway/run.py` correctly replaces `ctx.message` with a `build_resume_recovery_note()` system note for the **model**, but it persists the **original empty user message** to `state.db` via `_persist_user_message_override = ctx.message` (line 5818, set before the replacement).

Once that empty user row is in the transcript, the Pre-call sanitizer (`repair_empty_non_final_messages` in `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py`) heals it **in memory** on every subsequent API call — but the stored history is never mutated (by design). So the same empty message triggers the warning on **every turn** for the rest of the session's life.

## Impact

- 26 `Pre-call sanitizer: healed 1 empty non-final message(s)` warnings + 3 `Persisted transcript lagged live cached history` warnings in one QQ DM session over a ~2-hour window.
- The sanitizer prevents actual 400 errors (its job), so there is **no functional breakage** — but the session is permanently noisy in logs.
- The disk-vs-memory count offset (`disk=129, memory=130`) is also permanent for that session.

## Root cause

`gateway/run.py` line 5816–5833:

```python
if _is_resume_pending:
    _reason = getattr(_resume_entry, "resume_reason", None) or "restart_timeout"
    _persist_user_message_override = ctx.message   # ← line 5818: captures ORIGINAL empty text
    # ... adapter-awareness ...
    ctx.message = build_resume_recovery_note(       # ← replaces what the MODEL sees
        _reason, ctx.message, interactive=_interactive_resume,
    )
```

Then at line 5925–5926:

```python
if _persist_user_message_override is not None:
    _conversation_kwargs["persist_user_message"] = _persist_user_message_override
```

So the **recovery note goes to the model**, but the **empty string goes to the database**. The override is captured before the replacement.

## Evidence

### 1. Gateway log — empty message synthesized at restart

```
2026-08-14 05:58:49,503 INFO gateway.run: Scheduled auto-resume for 1 restart-interrupted session(s)
2026-08-14 05:58:49,855 INFO gateway.run: inbound message: platform=qqbot user=B74A939C8E1A66816031EE86D6F1C6F4 chat=B74A939C8E1A66816031EE86D6F1C6F4 msg='' reply_to_id=None reply_to_text=''
```

### 2. Database — empty user message persisted

```
sqlite3 state.db "SELECT id, role, length(content) AS clen FROM messages WHERE session_id='20260724_094354_caf1ed0c' AND role='user' AND (content='' OR content IS NULL);"

id      role  clen
106935  user  0
```

Timestamp: `2026-08-14 05:59:14` — exactly at the auto-resume window.

### 3. Sanitizer warnings — same session, 26 times over 2 hours

```
2026-08-14 19:14:30,606 WARNING [20260724_094354_caf1ed0c] run_agent: Pre-call sanitizer: healed 1 empty non-final message(s) by substituting placeholder content — ...
2026-08-14 20:46:18,586 WARNING [20260724_094354_caf1ed0c] run_agent: Pre-call sanitizer: healed 1 empty non-final message(s) ...
```

### 4. Disk-vs-memory lag — same session, offset is always +1

```
2026-08-14 19:14:30,522 WARNING [20260724_094354_caf1ed0c] gateway.run: Persisted transcript lagged live cached history for session agent:main:qqbot:dm:B74A939C8E1A66816031EE86D6F1C6F4 (disk=129, memory=130)
2026-08-14 20:36:37,934 WARNING [...] (disk=131, memory=132)
2026-08-14 20:38:17,124 WARNING [...] (disk=139, memory=140)
```

## Affected sessions

Five QQ DM sessions with the same empty-user-message pattern:

| Session | Source | Timestamp of empty user msg |
|---|---|---|
| `20260716_184517_caedbb` | qqbot | 2026-07-16 18:53:10 |
| `20260716_192100_97db90` | qqbot | 2026-07-16 18:53:10 |
| `20260716_192331_993eb8` | qqbot | 2026-07-16 18:53:10 |
| `20260716_194449_d51a00` | qqbot | 2026-07-16 18:53:10 |
| `20260724_094354_caf1ed0c` | qqbot | 2026-08-14 05:59:14 |

## Related issues

- #82924 — Pre-call sanitizer can emit an empty assistant message (tool_calls dedup → empty array). Different code path: that is about `sanitize_api_messages()` step 3 producing empty assistant `tool_calls`. This issue is about **persisting an empty USER message** from the gateway resume path.
- #76862 — Same tool_calls-dedup root cause as #82924, not the same as this one.

## Suggested fix

In the `_is_resume_pending` branch, persist the **recovery note** (or at minimum a non-empty placeholder) instead of the original empty `ctx.message`. For example, capture the override **after** the replacement:

```python
if _is_resume_pending:
    _reason = getattr(_resume_entry, "resume_reason", None) or "restart_timeout"
    ctx.message = build_resume_recovery_note(
        _reason, ctx.message, interactive=_interactive_resume,
    )
    _persist_user_message_override = ctx.message  # ← persist the note, not the empty original
```

This ensures the database row is non-empty and the sanitizer never needs to fire. The same change should apply to the safety-net branch at line 5864–5875.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent (latest main, Termux/Android)
- Provider: omniroute (custom OpenAI-compatible)
- Platform: qqbot (QQ DM)
- Daily gateway restart at 05:58 CST (Termux SIGKILL/OOM)

items.title: [Bug]: Truncated-response continuation (finish_reason=length) never checks for repetition before retrying, and Discord delivery has no split-count cap — one degenerate turn floods a channel with 30+ messages

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
### Bug Description

A single agent turn produced a final response of 60,698 characters, delivered to a live Discord channel as **31 separate messages** posted back-to-back. Reconstructed from `state.db` message rows and gateway logs, this happened in two independently-missing safety checks, not one:

1. **Generation side**: the model entered degenerate repetition mid-response, hit the provider's output-token ceiling (`finish_reason=length`), and Hermes's own truncation-continuation path retried it — appending a "continue, don't repeat" nudge — **without ever checking whether the content it was about to continue was already pathological**.
2. **Delivery side**: the resulting 60,757-char combined response was hard to miss (Discord's own 2000-char limit forces a split), yet the platform adapter splits and sends **every** resulting chunk with no upper bound on count.

Either check alone would have prevented the user-facing flood.

### Root Cause (confirmed against `main` @ `76d832d3`, Hermes Agent v0.20.0 / 2026.8.3, cross-checked against `state.db` message rows for the affected session)

**1. (Primary) `finish_reason=length` triggers an automatic continuation with zero content-sanity check on the truncated text.**

Evidence from `state.db` (`messages` table, `session_id='20260814_142129_1a77534b'`):

| id | role | len | finish_reason | timestamp (UTC) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 39020 | assistant | 57,752 | `length` | 14:56:05.907 |
| 39021 | user (synthetic) | 176 | — | 14:56:05.907 (same instant) |
| 39036 | assistant | 2,945 | `stop` | 14:58:24.877 |

`57752 + 2945 = 60697` ≈ the `60698`-char final response the gateway delivered — the two fragments were stitched into one turn.

Message 39020's content is not random garbage — it opens with `"We need to verify the model setting. The user wants ... Then '...' Then '...'"`: the model was narrating/summarizing the conversation so far, one prior user turn at a time. When it reached the point in history where the user had once said *"好，你幫我更改成 Google Gemini 4 31B。"* (said exactly **once**, at 14:33:33 — confirmed by scanning all 16 user-role rows in this session; there is no duplicate inbound message), it entered a token-level repetition loop echoing that fragment, verbatim, hundreds of times, consuming the rest of its output budget until the provider cut it off.

Message 39021 is Hermes's own auto-injected continuation nudge — `agent/conversation_loop.py:781-785` (`_LENGTH_CONTINUATION_OUTPUT_LIMIT`):
```python
_LENGTH_CONTINUATION_OUTPUT_LIMIT = (
    "[System: Your previous response was truncated by the output "
    "length limit. Continue exactly where you left off. Do not "
    "restart or repeat prior text. Finish the answer directly.]"
)
```
This fires from the `finish_reason == "length"` branch at `agent/conversation_loop.py:3196`. The branch already contains a specific, targeted sanity check for a *different* pathological case — thinking-budget exhaustion (`_thinking_exhausted`, `conversation_loop.py:3196-3260`) — which aborts immediately with a user-facing `"⚠️ Thinking Budget Exhausted"` message instead of retrying. **No equivalent check exists for "the truncated content is dominated by repeated text."** The continuation path (`conversation_loop.py:3369-3412`, guarded only by `length_continue_retries < 4` at line 1576/3333) unconditionally appends the truncated fragment to `messages` and asks the model to keep going. In this incident it only needed 1 of the 4 available retries — the second pass finished cleanly (`finish_reason=stop`, no further repetition) — so the retry-count ceiling never engaged; nothing else was in a position to catch the first fragment's content quality before it was folded into the final response.

**2. Delivery side: the chunk-send loop has no count/size ceiling either.**
`plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py:1002-1003`:
```python
MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH = 2000
_SPLIT_THRESHOLD = 1900  # near the 2000-char split point
```
`plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py:3114-3122`:
```python
# Format and split message if needed
formatted = self.format_message(content)
chunks = self.truncate_message(formatted, self.MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH)

message_ids = []
reference = self._reply_reference_for_send(reply_to, channel)

for i, chunk in enumerate(chunks):
```
`chunks` is iterated in full regardless of `len(chunks)`. No `if len(chunks) > N` guard exists here, in the structurally identical `_send_to_forum` path (line 3206), or the edit-overflow path (line 3473). A 2-chunk reply and a 200-chunk reply take the exact same code path.

**3. The gateway's own split-delivery bookkeeping already *knows* a split is happening, but only uses that for a duplicate-suppression decision, not a circuit breaker.**
`gateway/run.py:27059` (this incident's actual log line):
```
Stale streamed finalize detected for session %s on a multi-message split; skipping the in-place reconciliation edit and delivering the complete response via normal final send (#78541).
```
`_turn_split_delivery` (`gateway/run.py:27050-27059`) is a concrete, checked signal that the current response is being delivered as a multi-message split, available *before* the send happens. It is used only to pick edit-vs-fresh-send; never to ask "is this split unreasonably large?"

**4. Response-shape validation exists but only checks structural validity, not content sanity.**
`agent/conversation_loop.py:2786-2864` — `validate_response()` (dispatched per `api_mode`) checks for `response is None`, missing/empty `choices`, missing `content`, etc. A structurally well-formed response with `finish_reason=stop` and 60,698 chars of repeated text passes every check here.

**5. Contributing factor — the turn ran to 108K tokens across 10 API calls with no early exit.** Before producing the oversized answer, the agent spent ~15 minutes retrying blocked tool calls (`hermes model` requiring a TTY; an internal guard rejecting self-restart from inside the gateway process). Nothing in the retry/iteration accounting (turn ended at `api_calls=10/90`, well under budget) treats "many consecutive tool failures without task progress" as a signal to stop and hand back a short, controlled error instead of continuing to grow context — the polluted, 100K+-token context is the substrate the repetition loop in #1 happened on top of.

**6. Related, lower-confidence observation — not the cause of this incident, but same risk class.** `agent/background_review.py:3` documents that after most turns, `AIAgent.run_conversation` may fork a background self-review agent that replays the **full, unfiltered parent conversation snapshot** on the same model/runtime. `agent/background_review.py:757-758` shows the fork only inherits a `max_tokens` cap if the *parent* explicitly set one — no independent ceiling otherwise. In this incident the review fork for the same session was triggered 1.4s after the flood turn ended and was itself killed mid-call by a gateway restart (`Broken pipe` in the logs) before it produced anything — so it did not cause this flood, but it inherited the exact same 108K-token polluted snapshot and had no independent output-length guard either. Flagging as a related gap, not the root cause of this ticket.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Get a model into a state where, while narrating/summarizing prior conversation turns, it echoes one fragment repeatedly (long, error-laden context measurably increases the odds — see #5 above — but this is a model-degeneracy trigger, not a Hermes-specific one).
2. Let generation run to the provider's output-token ceiling (`finish_reason=length`) while still inside the repeated fragment.
3. Observe: `conversation_loop.py`'s length-continuation path retries automatically with no inspection of the truncated content (root cause #1).
4. Whether or not the continuation itself repeats, the stitched final response can already be tens of thousands of characters. Observe: the Discord adapter splits and sends **all** resulting chunks with no ceiling (root cause #2).

Root cause #2 alone is trivially reproducible without reproducing model degeneracy: call `DiscordAdapter.send()` with any string >60,000 chars against a live channel and count outbound messages.

### Actual Behavior

```
state.db: id=39020 role=assistant len=57752 finish_reason=length  (14:56:05.907 UTC)
state.db: id=39021 role=user     len=176   [System: ...truncated... Continue...] (same instant, synthetic)
state.db: id=39036 role=assistant len=2945  finish_reason=stop     (14:58:24.877 UTC)

gateway.run: response ready: platform=discord chat=1537828505927033063 time=882.3s api_calls=10 response=60698 chars
[Discord] Sending response (60757 chars) to 1537828505927033063
→ 31 individual Discord messages posted back-to-back
```

### Expected Behavior

1. In the `finish_reason == "length"` branch (`conversation_loop.py:3196`), before appending the continuation nudge, run a cheap content-sanity check on the truncated fragment (e.g. n-gram repetition ratio, or simply: longest exact substring repeated >K times) analogous to the existing `_thinking_exhausted` check at the same call site. On a pathological result, abort the turn with a short, user-facing error (same pattern as the existing `"⚠️ Thinking Budget Exhausted"` message) instead of continuing.
2. Independently, `DiscordAdapter.send()` (and the identical `_send_to_forum` / edit-overflow paths) should cap the number of chunks sent for one logical response — e.g. a configurable `max_split_messages` (suggested default: 5-8) — falling back to a short "response was abnormally large, see logs" notice instead of flooding.
3. The existing `_turn_split_delivery` bookkeeping in `gateway/run.py` already has the chunk context needed to enforce (2) platform-agnostically at the gateway layer instead of duplicating it per-adapter.

### Proposed Fix (sketch, for a follow-up PR)

1. Add a bounded repetition check (e.g. `agent/repetition_guard.py`, called from `conversation_loop.py:3196` right after `_thinking_exhausted` is ruled out) gating the length-continuation path.
2. Add `DiscordAdapter.MAX_SPLIT_MESSAGES` (or a shared constant in `gateway/platforms/base.py`) checked right after `chunks = self.truncate_message(...)` at `adapter.py:3116`, `3206`, `3473`.
3. Optionally surface `_turn_split_delivery`'s chunk count in `gateway/run.py` before calling adapter `send()` so (2) can be enforced once, platform-agnostically.

### Environment

- **Hermes Agent**: v0.20.0 (2026.8.3) · upstream commit `76d832d3857551a029c4b39c23945eb47c16fe5b`
- **Install method**: Docker (`nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest`)
- **Platform**: Discord (guild channel, non-forum, non-thread — plain `channel.send()` path)
- **Provider/model active during incident**: `nvidia` / `nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-omni-30b-a3b-reasoning` (verified against a same-day NVIDIA `/v1/models` snapshot — model ID itself was valid; this is not a "model doesn't exist" report)
- Verified via direct log + `state.db` inspection against the exact running commit (matched `hermes version` output to `git log -1` in a full clone of upstream at that commit).

### Related Work

- **#30408** — "Hermes should stop repeated tool loops and block obviously broken final responses." Closed 2026-06-28 as `completed`, **no linked PR**, maintainer (`teknium1`) declined the model-behavior framing verbatim: *"We don't want to fix models problems. There are also plenty of legitimate paths to repeat tool calls."* This report deliberately does not re-ask for model-output judgment. Root causes #1-#4 below are Hermes's own retry/validation/delivery code, independent of whether the model "should" have produced that output — the same distinction the maintainer's own closed **#10711** (below) already accepted for a structurally identical case.
- **#10711** — "Ollama returns `finish_reason='stop'` on truncated GLM responses, causing agent to silently drop final output" (closed, `completed`). Established the precedent that Hermes must not blindly trust a provider's finish-signal and needs its own content-side verification before treating a response as final. Root cause #1 in this report asks for the same class of check on the *other* side of that precedent: `finish_reason=length` is correctly detected, but the continuation path still doesn't inspect the truncated content before retrying.
- **#13208** (open, unresolved) + **#6784** / **#8528** (open PRs, unmerged: "tool loop detection with context pruning" / "integrate tool loop detection into agent loop") — cover contributing factor #5 (no-progress tool-call loops growing context unchecked). This report does not duplicate that ask; it references it only as background for why the turn reached 108K tokens before the repetition in #1 occurred. If #6784/#8528 land, they may reduce (but would not eliminate) exposure to #1 and #2 — the content-check and delivery-cap gaps are independent of whether the loop that grew the context gets shortened.
- **#78541** — "Suppressing normal final send swallows complete replies on Telegram group/forum sessions" (closed, fixed via #79669) — established the `_turn_split_delivery` flag this incident's payload traveled through. That fix addressed a *suppression* bug (legitimate content silently dropped); this report is the opposite direction (oversized content delivered with no ceiling) through the same code path.
- **#71643** — "Telegram streaming — successful finalize edit carries the stale preview text" (closed) — the stale-finalize reconciliation-edit fallback referenced in the same `gateway/run.py` block.
- **#25349** — "Discord streaming can duplicate final responses across chunked delivery" (open) — same general code area, different symptom (duplication vs. unbounded volume).
- **#75423** (open) — "`_SKILL_REVIEW_PROMPT` turns one-off investigations into documentation-shaped Skills" — a different symptom of the same background-review mechanism flagged as a related risk in root cause #6; corroborates that the review fork has more than one open edge case around what context/output it's trusted with.

### Additional Context

- No pending/queued outbound messages were involved — this was a single turn's response, delivered once, not a retry loop re-sending old content.
- The incident coincided with, but was not caused by, a global model configuration change and gateway restart the user performed shortly after (switching to `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b`, unrelated to the model active during the flood). Nothing in the user-facing output distinguished "this flood came from a turn already in flight" from "this flood came from the model you just switched to" — worth a documentation/UX note even outside this specific bug.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop auto-TTS reads the same reply again right after playback finishes

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Symptom

With `voice.auto_tts: true` ("Read responses aloud"), a reply is read aloud a **second time from the beginning** right after its playback finishes. Every spoken reply is affected.

## Reproduction

1. Enable read-responses-aloud (`voice.auto_tts: true` in config.yaml).
2. Send any prompt in the desktop chat and let the reply be read aloud to the end.
3. When playback finishes, the same reply starts playing again.

## Root cause (source trace, main @ b6726d57e)

Auto-speak dedupe is keyed on the renderer's message **row id**, which is volatile across the turn-end boundary:

1. `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-composer-voice.ts` — `lastSpokenIdRef` / `pendingResponse()` / `consumePendingResponse()` compare `last.id === lastSpokenIdRef.current`.
2. During streaming, the assistant row carries a live-tail id (`assistant-stream-*`; see `isLiveTailRow` in `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions/utils.ts`, which explicitly contrasts it with "a committed transcript row"). When the text completes, `speakLatest` in `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-auto-speak-replies.ts` marks **that** id spoken and starts playback.
3. At/after turn end, the authoritative flush reconciles the row via `reconcileResumeMessages()` — same bubble, same text, but the committed row's id replaces the `assistant-stream-*` id.
4. `use-auto-speak-replies.ts` also subscribes `$voicePlayback.listen(speakLatest)`. When playback ends, state transitions to `idle`, `speakLatest` fires, and `pendingResponse()` now sees the committed id ≠ `lastSpokenId` → the reply is treated as unspoken and played again. After the second playback the ids match, so it stops — which matches the observed "reads exactly twice" behavior.

### Sibling path with the same defect

The manual **Read Aloud** button (`apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/thread/assistant-message.tsx`, `ReadAloudButton`) calls `playSpeechText()` directly without marking the reply spoken. So manually reading the latest reply is likewise followed by an auto-speak replay on the playback-idle edge, whenever auto-speak hasn't already consumed that reply.

## Expected

Each completed reply is spoken at most once, regardless of live→committed row-id reconciliation or manual reads.

## Fix direction

Key spoken-state on something stable across the live→committed transition — e.g. the assistant role-ordinal of the turn, or a hash of the spoken text — or move spoken tracking into a shared per-session store that survives row identity changes; and have the manual read-aloud path mark the reply spoken too. Happy to discuss the exact key if a different invariant is preferred.

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop 0.17.0, built from main @ b6726d57e (local build, 2026-08-15)
- macOS (Apple Silicon)
- TTS provider: MiniMax (also reproducible in principle with any provider — the defect is in the renderer's dedupe key, not synthesis)

items.title: Add read-only repository context for issues and pull requests
items.body:
## User need

Hermes should be able to inspect the full issue and pull-request context of a selected repository so it can triage work and perform reviews with the relevant GitHub context.

## Requested scope

Add a configured repository allow-list and GitHub read-only metadata/contents access for those repositories:

- Issues: list, search, details, comments, labels, and milestones.
- Pull requests: list, search, details, changed files/diff, commits, review threads, and status checks.
- Pagination must cover the complete accessible result set; do not impose arbitrary small caps.

## Safety and privacy

- Least privilege: this capability must not comment, add/edit labels, assign, close/reopen, merge, push, dispatch workflows, or access/expose secrets.
- Never expose credentials in prompts, tool results, logs, errors, or UI.
- Private repositories are available only through an explicit app installation and repository allow-list.

## UX

Before acting, the agent should state which repositories and categories of data it will read. Missing or unavailable permissions should produce a clear, graceful explanation. Provide an obvious read-only smoke test.

## Acceptance

For one selected, allowed repository, Hermes can summarize open issues, open pull requests, and review context; mutation attempts are unavailable; and access is demonstrably limited to the configured repository scope.
